security_privacy_cost_impact: This increment writes the first TENANT DATA TABLES since batch 010, and their whole isolation rests on batch 011's helpers rather than on anything in this file -- which is the point of RFC-2026-020 §5/5 and the reason each of the four tables is exercised separately: a broken helper breaks all four identically, a wrong GRANT breaks one. Column-scoped grants throughout; `workspace_id` is absent from every UPDATE grant and `business_profile_id` from page_context_profiles', so no row can be moved across tenant or scope by an update even by a caller both halves of the policy would admit. `anon` is granted nothing anywhere, so an anonymous read is refused on the SCHEMA by the privilege system rather than filtered to zero rows. The two version tables grant no role UPDATE or DELETE at all, so §8.1's `N N N N N N` row is a privilege-layer denial and not a policy a later edit can widen. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: workspace lifecycle visibility. §8.5 lists it as part of a SELECT predicate and these policies do not carry it, so a member of a workspace in `access_blocked` can still read its business rows -- stated in the migration, in the manifest and here, and owed to an RFC plus batch 170. No secret, credential or customer datum is added; every fixture id is a synthetic uuid5. No cost impact.
migration_and_data_impact: Adds db/foundation/migrations/020_business.sql: four tables, ten policies, their column-scoped grants, four indexes and two updated_at triggers, plus an apply-time do-block that asserts the batch's own claims against the live catalog. It rewrites no merged migration -- migration invariant 1 -- and adds no cross-module foreign key, because §6's registry gives the business-channel/social FK to batch 111 and migration invariant 6 puts a cross-module FK in an integration batch. Every statement is idempotent (`create table if not exists`, `drop policy if exists` before each `create policy`, `create index if not exists`), so a re-run is a no-op rather than a failure. IT IS APPLIED IN CI ONLY and deliberately NOT applied to the provisioned Supabase instance: 020 depends on 011, which is itself declared not applied there, and a batch cannot be applied to a database missing the batch it is built on. The committed snapshot therefore declares 020 by name in not_applied_to_this_instance, takes its digest over the applied set, and records no row in tenant_tables for a table that is not there.
compatibility_impact: Additive at the database. No existing table, column, policy or grant is altered, so batch 010's and 011's behaviour is unchanged. Three repository-level shapes DO change and are called out: `FIXTURE_SQL` in tests/db/identity/run-isolation.mjs becomes `FIXTURE_SQL_FILES`, an ordered list -- the two readers (that file and scripts/db/rls-smoke.mjs) both move, and no stale singular is left to be loaded by mistake; the isolation cases gain a fifth outcome kind, `rejected`, which REQUIRES a SQLSTATE and refuses 42501; and `catalogLint`'s two per-tenant-table loops become one exported `tenantTableLint` that additionally checks the completeness of the list itself.
known_limitations: CI PROVES THE POLICIES, NEVER THE PLATFORM. The container's roles come from db/foundation/ci/supabase-shim.sql and were created by us; a green run means the policies still do what they did, not that this holds on Supabase. Unchanged by this batch and repeated because batch 020's tables inherit it whole.

THE ATTRIBUTE SURFACE OF A BUSINESS PROFILE IS ONE `name`. §5 names no column of these tables and forbids 'metadata', 'config', 'payload' and 'JSON' without a declared JSON Schema version, maximum size, prohibited fields and owner -- none of which exists. The industry pack is batch 030 and knowledge is 040, so each adds its typed columns to the current row and the matching column to the version row in one change. That is what 'current + immutable versions' costs, and it is cheaper than a document column nobody can validate.

NO current_version_id POINTER on either current row. It would be a circular foreign key needing a deferred constraint, and §6's registry puts 'deferred FK' in batch 021. `version_number`, unique per parent, answers 'which version is latest' without one.

WORKSPACE LIFECYCLE VISIBILITY IS NOT ENFORCED ON BATCH 020's TABLES, and this is the one gap in the batch that is a gap rather than a refusal. Closing it needs either a join to app.workspaces from these policies -- which would make the width of business visibility a property of another module's policy set, the exact coupling RFC-2026-020 §5/5 removed for membership -- or a lifecycle-aware helper owned by app_authz, whose grants §6.1/6 pins to USAGE on schema app and a column-scoped SELECT on four columns of app.workspace_members and which authzLint rejects any widening of. Owed to an RFC plus batch 170.

§8.6 CASES 3 AND 4 ARE OWED BY BATCH 021, and now for a narrower reason than when batch 010 wrote them off. The tables exist and both businesses are in workspace A; what does not exist is the row that would narrow a member to one of them. Batch 020 asserts the current state positively so that 021 has to change a test to change it.

NO CHANNEL BINDING TABLE, though §5's inventory row for this module reads 'page_context_profiles, versions, bindings'. A binding carries social_account_id, whose table is batch 110, and §6's registry gives the business-channel/social foreign key to batch 111. The registry's own description of 020 -- 'business/page + immutable versions' -- omits bindings for that reason. Owed by 110/111.

NO COMMAND FUNCTION AND NO app_command GRANT. The data package specifies no command surface for business.core, and a grant issued ahead of the thing that needs it is a grant nobody reviews against a caller. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a client holding INSERT on a version table can write a version whose content never was the current row's content. Binding the two into one transaction is what a command function is for, and it is the command surface -- not RLS -- that owes it.

reviewer_instructions: Read db/foundation/migrations/020_business.sql top to bottom before anything else. Its header states which §8.1 cells are implemented, which are REFUSED and why, and what is not implemented at all -- if any of those three lists is wrong, the batch is wrong regardless of what the tests say.

The four things worth adversarial attention:
(1) THE EDITOR CELL. §8.1 marks Business/Page INSERT/UPDATE `P` for editor and this batch denies it. Decide whether refusing to invent a capability set is right, or whether the editor should have been granted; `editor-a-cannot-create-a-business` is the case that changes if you disagree.
(2) THE ARCHIVE PREDICATE. page_context_profiles' INSERT policy is the ONE predicate in the file that reads another table. Satisfy yourself the direction is fail-closed -- the subquery runs as the caller, so app.business_profiles's own SELECT policy applies to it -- and that narrowing §8.1's unconditional Y by §11.3 is the right reading.
(3) THE `rejected` OUTCOME KIND. It exists so §4 invariant 10 can be asserted about a CONSTRAINT rather than about any error. Check that it cannot be satisfied by 42501, and that the case using it inserts version_number 2 -- version 1 would hit the unique index first and return 23505, which is a different control passing under this one's name.
(4) THE COMPLETENESS RULE in scripts/db/run.mjs. It is new, it is what forces 020's tables into the snapshot the day the instance receives the batch, and it is the part of this diff least related to business/page. Construct a snapshot with a row removed and one with a row added and check both are refused.
